definition: The standard expansion bus that connects GPUs, network cards and SSDs to a host CPU. A 16-lane (x16) link carries about 64 GB/s in total on Gen4, 128 GB/s on Gen5 and 256 GB/s on Gen6, both directions combined.

An open standard that runs over PCIe wiring and adds cache-coherent memory access, so CPUs can use memory expanders or share memory with accelerators. It is the open-standard alternative to proprietary coherent links such as NVLink-C2C.

A programming model in which CPU and GPU share one virtual address space, so the same pointer works on both. With a coherent link (NVLink-C2C) the GPU reads CPU memory directly; over PCIe the driver must migrate pages, which is much slower.

Moving the attention cache (KV cache) of idle or long conversations out of scarce GPU HBM into cheaper CPU memory or storage, then reloading it when the user returns instead of recomputing it from scratch.
The software pipeline, usually running on host CPU cores, that reads training samples from storage, decodes and augments them and hands batches to the GPUs. If it is slower than the GPUs, they wait.
GPUs sitting idle because the host cannot supply data, launch kernels or return tool results fast enough; it shows up as low GPU utilization even though the GPUs themselves are not the bottleneck.
NVIDIA's Data Loading Library, which moves image, video and audio decoding and augmentation from the host CPU onto the GPU to prevent data-loading bottlenecks.

A CPU feature that runs two (or more) hardware threads on one core by letting them share its execution units, raising total throughput at the cost of less predictable per-thread speed. Intel calls it Hyper-Threading.

NVIDIA's name for the two-threads-per-core scheme in its Vera CPU; NVIDIA describes it as dividing each core's resources between the two threads to make per-thread performance more predictable than conventional SMT.

An isolated environment (typically a container or small virtual machine pinned to a CPU core) in which an AI agent's generated code, browser session or tool call runs, or in which reinforcement-learning attempts are executed and scored.
